A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Online Decision-Focused Learning with matching algorithms, experiments, and appendices A–G. All 38 pages of v2 and 34 pages of v3 support comparison through readable text, equations, and figures.

before.justification: v2 reports original synthetic item-selection experiments in Section 4 and a model-misspecification study in Appendix E, including Figures 1 and 3.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds results for an 80-item problem in Appendix E, Figure 4.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 retain the same regularized losses, log-barrier/entropy choices, approximate-oracle calls, FTPL perturbations, and randomized-gradient updates. v3 clarifies the distinction between played and smoothed decisions without changing these procedures.

E1.justification: Appendix E adds selection among 80 candidate items alongside the existing 5-item problem, expanding the tested input and decision-space dimensionality. The synthetic domain, item-selection task, and misspecification scenarios otherwise remain unchanged.

E2.justification: PF-OGD and online SPO remain the comparison methods in Figure 1 and also appear in the new Figure 4. The misspecification study still compares DF-OGD with PF-OGD; no comparator is added, removed, or substantively revised.

E3.justification: The added 80-item configuration in Figure 4 displays roughly 2,000 timesteps, whereas the retained main experiment uses 5 items and T=5,000. The original data-generation settings, cost/MSE metrics, and T=1,000 misspecification protocol remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The new higher-dimensional experiment tests whether the methods remain effective when the candidate set grows to 80 items. This adds a limited scaling analysis; the existing gamma-based sensitivity study of model misspecification is unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report 10 runs and 95% confidence intervals for the main comparison, with Appendix E describing Gaussian intervals, and 50 runs for the misspecification study. v3 reports no changed run counts, seed practices, or new statistical procedure.

E6.justification: Figure 4 adds cost and prediction-error curves for 80 items: DF-OGD and DF-FTPL achieve lower decision costs than PF-OGD and online SPO while exhibiting higher prediction errors. Figures 1 and 3 retain identical plotted results, so this is additional evidence under different conditions.

T1.justification: v3 excludes beta=0 from H2 and substantially revises the margin-integral derivation and Lemmas 2 and 6, introducing alpha^beta-dependent approximation bounds. Theorem 1 changes its dependence on the number of faces from n^(1/2) to n^(3/2). H1 and path-length indexing are also revised. These affect central guarantees, although some downstream formulas retain the earlier bounds.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and principal conclusion retain the claims of introducing online DFL, providing static and dynamic regret guarantees for DF-FTPL and DF-OGD, and outperforming the same two empirical baselines. The added evidence and future directions do not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: v3 discusses potentially faster rates through discretization and expert aggregation at an unfavorable dimensional cost, and identifies general convex feasible sets as future work. Appendix B adds an argument that downstream optimization may dominate oracle costs. Appendix E interprets Figure 4 as evidence of effectiveness in moderately high dimensions.

D1.justification: The data-generation recipe, PyTorch implementation disclosure, oracle warm starts and 10 SGD steps at learning rate 0.01, and baseline tuning information are retained. v3 supplies no substantive new implementation instructions, hardware/runtime measurements, or code/data access information.

R1.justification: v3 adds Rakhlin, Sridharan, and Tewari (2011) and explicitly positions the framework as a stochastic-adversary setting in Section 2. The broader DFL and online bilevel positioning remains largely unchanged; conversion to author-year citations does not constitute additional related work.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites clarify the sequential game, conditional regret comparator, approximate oracle, and algorithm descriptions. Sections 1–5 and appendices A–G retain their organization. Author affiliations and citation style change, and an acknowledgment section is added.

P2.justification: The document is reformatted throughout into the ICLR template, changing the title/author block, affiliation placement, running headers, typography, text width, and display sizing and placement. Figure 4 is added; Figures 1–3 retain their underlying content.

improvement.justification: The 80-item experiment and clearer framework description add useful evidence and explanation. v3 also corrects part of v2's margin-integral reasoning, but the revised alpha^beta bounds are not consistently propagated: Appendix G.4 returns to the earlier expression after Equation (53), and G.5 retains it in Equation (59), while beta-independent T^(-1/4) guarantees remain. These inconsistencies concern the paper's central theoretical contribution, making the net quality effect of the partial corrections and empirical additions unclear.
